subject: Expansion: burst credits & tiered per-token discounts
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Joe Kim <joe.kim@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expansion: burst credits & tiered per-token discounts

Hi Sally —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Joe and I reviewed your Q1 usage snapshot and I think we have a clear path to support both the new Search-Assist product and the Marketing personalization team without disrupting your current commit. Two quick things I wanted to confirm before I put a formal proposal together:

1) Expected steady-state tokens/month for Search-Assist (inference only) once in production — you mentioned ~120M tokens/month but would love a concise number range (80-150M?).
2) Whether you want the burst buffer to be applied at the org level or scoped to the Search-Assist product during ramp.

If you can confirm those, I’ll share a pricing construct that blends: incremental commit + short-term burst credits + a tiered per-token discount schedule for higher volumes.

Also attaching the usage snapshot you shared (I exported the CSV for our pricing model).

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137
Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_snapshot_q1.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Sally Park <sally.park@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion: burst credits & tiered per-token discounts

Camila —

Thanks, and great recap. Quick answers below:

1) Search-Assist expected range is 90-140M tokens/month during steady state. We should plan for the upper end for safety.
2) Prefer burst credits scoped to Search-Assist for the first 90 days; we can revisit org-level burst after we see traffic patterns.

A few asks from procurement before we get to commit sizes: can you show an example of how incremental commits ladder into lower per-token rates (example tiers + math)? Also, we need a short statement that burst credits are non-refundable and expire after 90 days.

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow to walk through numbers if that helps.

—Sally
Sally Park
Dir. Product, Acme Analytics
Sally.Park@acmeanalytics.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@acmeanalytics.com>, Joe Kim <joe.kim@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion: burst credits & tiered per-token discounts

Sally —

Thanks for the confirmations. I’ve put together a simple worked example in the attached SOW and summarized the math below so procurement can digest quickly:

Example (monthly tokens):
- Baseline committed tokens: 200M (this covers current teams + Search-Assist steady-state at upper end)
- Incremental commit tranche: +100M tokens/month for a 12-month add-on
- Per-token pricing (hosted API):
  - 0–200M: $0.00012/token
  - 200M–400M: $0.000095/token (tiered discount applied to marginal tokens above 200M)
  - >400M: custom pricing (we can extend tiers if you anticipate that)
- Burst credits: we can provide a 90-day scoped burst buffer equal to 25% of the incremental tranche (for Search-Assist only). Burst credits expire after 90 days and are non-refundable — I’ll include the exact language in the SOW.

I’m looping in Ben (pricing) to confirm whether we have flexibility on the marginal tier and if we can offer introductory credits for the first 60 days as a short-term incentive.

If that looks reasonable, I’ll formalize the SOW with the attachments and DocuSign link for signatures.

—Camila

Attachments: Acme_Expansion_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion: burst credits & tiered per-token discounts

Camila —

Reviewed the proposal notes. A couple of internal points before we lock numbers:

- Marginal tier at $0.000095 is doable for a 12-month 100M increment, but we should gate the rate on a quarterly usage review and a minimum monthly commit ACH to protect unit economics. Suggest adding an SLA clause: "usage review at 90 days with option to renegotiate if actual sustained usage deviates >25% from committed volume."
- Introductory incentive: we can offer a one-time 15% credit applied to the first-month token bill (not to burst credits) as sign-on. This needs approval from Finance but is within precedent for strategic expansion deals.
- Legal will want the burst-credit expiration language explicit; propose: "Burst credits are non-refundable, non-transferable, and expire 90 days from issuance."

If you want to be aggressive, we could front-load an extra 10% of burst credits for the first 30 days only, but only if Acme signs the incremental commit within 14 days of proposal. That could be our ask in the DocuSign cover note.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal: incremental commit + scoped burst credits (next steps)

Sally / Joe —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround. Attached is a concise proposal and SOW that reflects the items we discussed: incremental 100M tokens/month for 12 months, tiered marginal pricing with the 200M–400M tier at $0.000095/token, a 25% scoped burst buffer for Search-Assist (90-day expiration), and a one-time 15% first-month credit. Key next steps:

1) Review SOW (attached) — let me know any legal/PO language you need added.
2) If acceptable, sign the DocuSign (link below) within 14 days to receive the front-loaded extra 10% burst credits for the first 30 days.
3) After signature, we’ll schedule a 30/60/90 usage review cadence (owner: Acme Product) and set the billing start date to the first of the next month.
